label: Roofing
tone: practical and reassuring, with clear urgency after storm damage or an active leak
local_angle: What drives roof damage varies sharply by region: in Hail Alley (the Colorado Front Range, Texas, Oklahoma, Kansas, Nebraska) frequent severe hailstorms are the single biggest cause of roof claims, sometimes requiring full replacement after one storm; in the Gulf Coast and Southeast, high humidity, UV exposure, and hurricane-force wind drive granule loss and wind-lifted shingles; in northern snow-load regions, ice dams and heavy snow accumulation stress roof structures and cause winter leaks; and in the Southwest, intense sustained UV exposure shortens shingle lifespan through heat-driven brittleness.
seasonal_calendar: Spring is peak season for storm/hail damage inspections and insurance claims following winter and spring storm systems. Summer brings UV-driven wear and is the most common time for full replacements and new installations (dry weather, long work days). Fall is the preferred window for preventive maintenance and gutter work before winter. Winter brings emergency leak repairs and ice dam issues in colder regions.
